findings.bites_when: Now for log wipe/poison/disk-fill via text/plain POSTs (reproduced). Becomes a source-tree write the moment any POST write route is added (the S2-08 authoring-kit draft/accept flow is the obvious candidate), or anyone sets server.host/allowedHosts to true to test on a phone or a friend's machine.
findings.disconfirm: Probed rather than assumed. Path traversal: every encoded/backslash/dotdot id rejected. Body cap: a chunked 300 KB body with no Content-Length got 413. Host: rebinding Host header got 403 because Vite 8 registers hostValidationMiddleware before configureServer hooks (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:25058 vs 25064). Cross-origin PUT/DELETE: the OPTIONS reply carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the evil origin, so a browser blocks the real request. Only simple POSTs (text/plain, no preflight) get through. Chrome's Private Network Access may block public-to-localhost fetches on some versions; not relied on.
findings.recommendation: In the middleware, before reading the body: reject any request whose Origin header is present and not exactly http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://localhost:<port>; require Content-Type: application/json on POST/PUT; require a per-run random token (generated in configureServer, injected into index.html via transformIndexHtml, sent as a custom header, which also forces a preflight); assert Host equals the bound address instead of trusting Vite. Also destroy the request once the cap is exceeded (readRequestBody keeps consuming the whole stream), and have GET asset routes use lstat and refuse symlinks (probe: a stages/evil.json symlink to /etc/hosts echoed '##\n# Host' in the parse error).
findings.ignore_cost: A drive-by page can erase your session log today and can write into the repo through the first write route you add later.

findings.bites_when: When browser telemetry is wired and a session reaches the 50 MiB trigger: every pass freezes the dev server (HMR and all bridge routes) for about a second per 50 MiB, rising with the compacted file, which is re-parsed and re-stringified whole each time; if 50 MiB lands inside the 60 s window it repeats on every batch. Disk full: appendFileSync throws after sequence was already advanced, the handler reports it as HTTP 400 'Bad request' and nothing retries or surfaces it. A killed process mid-append leaves a line with no newline, and the next append is concatenated onto it, destroying one valid record (code reading, not probed).
findings.disconfirm: The compacted file is written before the active file, so a crash between them duplicates events rather than losing them, and the rename-based writeAtomic prevents half-written files; both are good. I did not run a 500 MiB case (a read-parse-join of that size is near V8's string limit and several GB of heap); treat the 500 MiB cap as unvalidated.
findings.recommendation: Switch to size-rotated segments (log.0001.jsonl ...) with a tiny in-memory index, so compaction becomes 'summarise the oldest segment, delete it' and never rewrites the world; prefix every append with a newline guard; map ENOSPC to a visible warning and a dropped-count record rather than a 400. Lower the caps to what a session really needs (a few tens of MiB) and fix the skill sentence to say eviction can drop old warn/error records.
findings.ignore_cost: Telemetry becomes a periodic multi-second stall of the dev server exactly when sessions get long enough to matter.

keep.claim: Path handling in the bridge is genuinely tight: ids are whitelist-matched, percent signs, slashes and backslashes rejected before any join, and the resolved target is checked for containment. Every traversal probe (%2f, %5c, %2e%2e, a/../b, uppercase, dotfile, save-slot variants) was rejected, and writes go through temp file plus rename so a symlink at the target is replaced, not followed.
The server binds to loopback only and relies on Vite 8's allowedHosts check, which rejected a spoofed Host header with 403 in a real probe. Keep host: '127.0.0.1' and do not set allowedHosts: true.

The compactor's design is sound on durability ordering (compacted file written before active, atomic rename) and its eviction-tier rule is explicit, tested, and deterministic; a crash between the two writes duplicates rather than loses events.

The suite is fast (133 tests in about 1.9 s, 2.7 s wall) with no snapshot tests; grep-based architecture tests (layer boundaries, no exemplar ids in domain/application) are cheap and catch the exact drift P1 worries about.

unconsidered_routes.title: Log nothing, replay: deterministic reproduction instead of always-on AI tracing
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Because the sim is meant to be seeded and fixed-step, the scripted command log plus seed is a complete record of a run (this is already accepted as the golden-test artifact, R3C1). Keep production telemetry to crash/warn, frame-time spikes and a state hash every N frames. When a bug appears, replay the command log with a trace sink enabled, and have the replay stop at the first hash divergence or at a chosen tick. Decision traces then cost zero disk in normal play and can be as verbose as wanted on replay.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Factorio and Starcraft-style deterministic replays with desync hash checkpoints; Dwarf Fortress-style reproduce-from-seed debugging; the rr record-and-replay debugger idea.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Replaces the 'every AI trace logs' rule in AGENTS.md and most of the 50/500 MiB machinery; telemetry stops being a second copy of the Act log.

unconsidered_routes.title: Minimal eval/ shape with a one-way ownership rule
unconsidered_routes.proposal: One harness, src/application/headless/runScenario(fixture, script, seed, pacing) returns {worldStateHashes, actLog, observations}. tests/golden/ calls it for 2-3 short scripts and compares committed hash files (verify, under 1 s). eval/ holds eval/cases/*.case.json (fixture id, seed list, script, assertions as data), eval/assertions/ (a registry of evidence_coverage, diffusion_bounds, text_gate_pool, and so on), eval/run.ts, and eval/out/ (gitignored). Exact-answer, one-seed, millisecond checks stay in tests/. Anything over many seeds, over the real content pack, or reporting a distribution goes in eval/. Fitted tables live in data/fitted/*.json with the rules hash inside; one fast test in tests/ asserts every fitted table's hash equals the current rulesHash, and `npm run eval:ai -- --refit` regenerates them. Text gates: the pure gateLine(brief, text) function and about ten adversarial cases live in tests/; eval/ only runs it over the whole pool for coverage and duplication metrics.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Golden master tests plus separate benchmark suites (the Rust compiletest versus perf-suite split); Factorio's replay-based CI.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Defines 05f scope so its first smoke case reuses the golden harness instead of re-implementing a headless rollout, and gives the S2-08 authoring kit an obvious home for pool-corpus metrics.

unconsidered_routes.title: Per-run token and Origin lock for every dev-server write route
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Generate a random token in configureServer, inject it into the served page via transformIndexHtml, and have the bridge require it as a custom header plus an exact Origin match. All future write routes (authoring-kit accept, stage-lab saves) register through one guarded helper, so a new route cannot be added unauthenticated.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Vite's own server.fs.strict and Host validation response to CVE-2025-24010; Next.js dev-server origin allowlist.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Replaces the per-route ad hoc checks; a registerBridgeRoute(method, path, handler) wrapper becomes the only way to add a route.

unconsidered_routes.title: Single-purpose crash box instead of a general session log
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Split the debug channel in two: a small ring buffer of the last N seconds of structured events kept in memory in the browser and flushed to logs/crash-<timestamp>.json on any error or on demand via a key, and a separate opt-in trace file for deliberate investigation. Normal play writes nothing to disk.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Flight-recorder buffers in Chromium tracing and Unreal's crash reporter context log.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Replaces continuous NDJSON streaming and rolling compaction with something that cannot grow without bound or stall the dev server.
